source.title: NU-AIR - A Neuromorphic Urban Aerial Dataset for Detection and Localization of Pedestrians and Vehicles
source.authors: Craig Iaboni; Thomas Kelly; Pramod Abichandani

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains neural networks from random initialization and reports performance on a new dataset, but its reported metric is test-set detection mAP, not training classification error. Its depth ablation also compares SNN test mAP, not training error.
record.gate_note: Training-from-random-initialization is stated for DNNs and SNNs. The reported outcomes are test-set mAP, runtime, sparsity, and ablation comparisons; no training classification error or training loss outcomes are reported. Include only results that measure training choices covered by the versions, while noting that test mAP cannot establish whether those versions' training-error effects occurred.
record.test_reason: The study uses Kaiming initialization and batch normalization in object detectors but reports test-set detection mAP and inference efficiency. It does not measure training error, convergence speed, trainable depth, local minima, or learning-rate stability. The depth and normalization ablations therefore do not test V3 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors present an open-source annotated aerial event dataset and baseline detection evaluations. They emphasize that SNN results are comparable to matching networks on other event datasets, while drone-induced visual artifacts and event-data sparsity pose challenges. Their comparative analysis also reports higher average test mAP for DNNs than SNNs.
record.recipe_differences: Models are trained from random initialization on the NU-AIR detection dataset; outcomes are detection mAP on its test set rather than training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Test mAP changes with SNN architecture size, bias removal, dropout, pooling type, and normalization type.

fits_no_version.finding: Randomly initialized detectors achieve average test mAP of 0.41 for DNNs and 0.16 for SNNs on NU-AIR; reported runtimes measure inference processing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Detector architecture affects test detection performance and inference efficiency on NU-AIR.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller MobileNet, VGG, and DenseNet variants reduce test mAP by 8%, 6%, and 6%, respectively; larger variants show no gains over baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing SNN depth beyond the tested baselines does not improve NU-AIR test detection mAP.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing BatchNorm with LayerNorm reduces test mAP by 6% for DenseNet and VGG and 16% for MobileNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BatchNorm yields higher NU-AIR test detection mAP than LayerNorm in the tested SNN configurations.

record.problems: The reported performance measures are test-set mAP rather than training error. The depth and normalization comparisons are presented as figure-referenced percentage changes without underlying numeric table values in the supplied text. The paper notes data from a single New Jersey city and that SNNs were evaluated on GPU hardware rather than target neuromorphic hardware.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported results are test-set detection performance or efficiency measures and do not report the training-error or training-dynamics outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error, including on CIFAR with clean or randomized labels, is not reported.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or measurement of spurious local minima.
Depth ablations report test mAP, without training-error comparisons, longer-training controls, or identity-shortcut comparisons.
Kaiming initialization is used without comparing initializations, signal propagation, learning speed, or trainable depth.
No stability-threshold, curvature, sharpness, loss-recovery, or divergence experiment.
BatchNorm versus LayerNorm is evaluated by test mAP, without training-speed, learning-rate-tolerance, normalization-free, or Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V3 and V6 statuses to not_tested. Speculation about optimization difficulties in deeper networks does not establish training degradation from test mAP alone. The empty row set is appropriate; no omitted result measures a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: No training classification error is reported; no CIFAR benchmarks, corrupted labels, random labels, or early-stopping comparison.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or neuron-width comparison.
The paper varies SNN architecture depth and reports test mAP, but not training error or whether runs stalled; it does not compare plain networks with identity shortcuts.
Kaiming uniform initialization is specified for SNN convolutions, but there is no initialization comparison or reported training speed/depth outcome.
No learning-rate stability threshold, curvature, sharpness, or recovery/divergence experiment.
Batch normalization is compared with layer normalization for SNNs, but only test mAP is reported; no training speed or learning-rate tolerance outcome is reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study uses the optimization methods in detector training but reports detection performance and inference efficiency, without testing the outcomes specified by V1–V6.

tranche.reason: Sections 4.1–4.3 use gradient training, Kaiming initialization and batch normalization for object detectors. Depth and normalization ablations report detection mAP rather than training error, convergence speed, trainable depth or learning-rate stability.

source_check.notes: No rows, statements or verdicts were listed. The depth and normalization ablations do not establish support for or challenges to the claim versions.
